result.title: Sonny-ENS: demystifying machine-learning ensemble weather forecasting
result.comment: 25 pages, 6 figures, 7 Extended Data figures and 3 Extended Data tables; Supplementary Information (4 figures, 2 tables) included
result.summary: Every weather forecast is uncertain, and decisions from flood warnings to energy trading depend on how well that uncertainty is quantified. Machine-learning (ML) ensembles now quantify it better than the best physics-based ensemble, yet two things about them remain opaque: whether their skill requires hundreds to thousands of accelerator-days of training, and how a network with a simple source of randomness produces a spread that follows the flow. Here we introduce Sonny-ENS, an ensemble of three 68.9-million-parameter networks with Monte Carlo dropout, trained on the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) in 2.7 A40 GPU-days. On 2022, it has a lower CRPS than the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts ensemble (ENS) on 96% of 570 targets and an 8.3% lower mean CRPS at lead times of 1-10 days. It outperforms the operational GenCast on 69% of the targets, and a 51-member, 15-day forecast takes 69 s on one GPU. Ablations identify the ingredients of this skill, and a Kolmogorov-Arnold sparse autoencoder shows that dropout injects uncertainty mainly in the tropics, whereas the spread grows where the atmosphere is baroclinically unstable (spatial correlation 0.91 with the Eady growth rate). Skillful probabilistic weather forecasts are therefore within reach of a single GPU server.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 Sonny-ENS：三个约 6900 万参数网络加 Monte Carlo dropout，以 CRPS 为目标训练，用单 GPU 数天训练即得到优于业务集合的 ML 天气预报，并用稀疏自编码器分析 dropout 产生的离散度在空间上的分布。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「简单随机源产生多样化样本、再定位不确定性落在何处」的机制，可能与 LVR 中多种 latent 假设的采样与贡献、位置归因问题形成类比线索，可供核查，但任务与模态差距较大。
